lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Replace the phone number and website if they are placeholders.
items.because: A reviewer needs working contact details.

items.says: Use a professional profile or portfolio link.
items.because: It would let a reviewer verify your work.

items.says: Specify whether the 35% accuracy improvement is relative or a percentage-point change.
Give the evaluation set or metric behind the accuracy result.
items.because: The reader needs enough context to judge the evaluation.

items.says: Explain what was validated in the tool-use trajectories.
items.because: The terminology may be unclear to a general ML reviewer.

items.says: Clarify what reviewer disagreement measures.
Clarify whether the change from 14% to 6% is in percentage points or relative terms.
Explain what in-scope signals means.
items.because: That boundary may be important to understanding your contribution.

items.says: State the evaluation conditions or scale for the latency and tool-call improvements.
items.because: The improvements need to be interpretable.

items.says: Confirm that equal accuracy is supported by a defined evaluation.
items.because: Otherwise it may be an informal observation.

items.says: Clarify what counted as an accuracy regression.
Clarify what release or decision the checks informed.
items.because: That context may not be obvious to the target audience.

items.says: The bullet repeats the fine-tuning method in the first bullet.
items.because: It adds no measurable result.

items.says: Be precise about how loss masking enabled the model to reproduce tool outputs.
items.because: Assistant-only loss masking typically excludes non-assistant tokens from the training loss.

items.says: The backlog reduction is duplicated under the Research-Agent project.
items.because: The accomplishment should not be counted twice.

items.says: Make the time window for the backlog reduction clearer.
items.because: The reader needs to be able to judge the 68% result.

items.says: Clarify how the backlog reduction was measured.
items.because: The reader needs to be able to judge the 68% result.

items.says: Add context on how the GPU-memory reduction was measured.
Say whether model quality or training behavior was maintained.
items.because: A reviewer may wonder about the trade-off.

items.says: Specify the load-test conditions or workload if they materially affect the result.
items.because: Otherwise, the latency numbers are hard to compare with other systems.

items.says: Maintained and adds have inconsistent tenses.
Explain what the three-day release cycle is measured against.
Use wording that reflects your contribution to implementing the checks.
items.because: Maintained alone understates that contribution.

items.says: Make the operational result more measurable.
items.because: Removing nightly backlogs does not show how often or how much dispatch was affected.

items.says: Substantiate or remove the broad AI-first adoption claim.
items.because: Adoption, faster delivery, and improved outcomes need concrete evidence.

items.says: Explain what working context means.
Explain how the 100x conversation growth was measured.
Add a comparison or quality constraint for the token reduction.
items.because: The reader needs to know whether it preserved useful performance.

items.says: State the test conditions behind 50-way fan-out.
Explain how you verified that deadlocks and lost results were eliminated.
items.because: This would make the reliability improvement more credible.

items.says: Clarify your specific contribution to integrating the metrics.
items.because: Integrated alone leaves the degree of ownership unclear.

items.says: Say whether others used the metrics or the project adopted them, if available.
Clarify what the Kendall correlation was calculated against.
items.because: The statistic needs a clear interpretation.

items.says: Explain how the 400-plus trials were structured.
items.because: The statistic needs a clear interpretation.

items.says: The bullet duplicates the diagnostics-branch achievement under the internship.
items.because: The same signals and backlog result should not appear as a separate project accomplishment.

items.says: Git is listed as a programming language.
items.because: Git is a tool.

items.says: Kubernetes does not fit naturally in the ML & Agents category.
items.because: The skills need clearer groupings.

items.says: Use a consistent spelling convention for penalises.
items.because: It uses British spelling while the résumé otherwise appears oriented toward U.S. roles.
